title: Threading Create Thread
code:
import threading
import time

def worker(name: str, delay: float):
    print(f"{name} started")
    time.sleep(delay)
    print(f"{name} finished")

# Create thread:
t = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=("Thread-A", 2), daemon=False)
t.start()  # Start execution

# Wait for completion:
t.join()
print("Main thread: done")

# Multiple threads:
threads = []
for i in range(5):
    t = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(f"Thread-{i}", 1))
    threads.append(t)
    t.start()

for t in threads:
    t.join()

print("All threads completed")

# Thread with run method:
class MyThread(threading.Thread):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name=name)
    
    def run(self):
        print(f"{self.name} is running")

mt = MyThread("CustomThread")
mt.start()
mt.join()
explanation: threading.Thread creates threads. start() begins execution, join() waits for completion.

title: Threading Event
code:
import threading
import time

# Event for signaling:
stop_event = threading.Event()

def worker():
    while not stop_event.is_set():
        print("Working...")
        time.sleep(0.5)
    print("Worker stopped")

t = threading.Thread(target=worker, daemon=True)
t.start()

time.sleep(2)
print("Main: signaling stop")
stop_event.set()  # Signal worker to stop
t.join()

# Wait with timeout:
def waiter(event, timeout):
    print("Waiting...")
    if event.wait(timeout):
        print("Event was set!")
    else:
        print("Timed out waiting")

ready = threading.Event()
t = threading.Thread(target=waiter, args=(ready, 3))
t.start()
time.sleep(1)
ready.set()  # wakes waiter

# Multiple workers waiting:
start_gate = threading.Event()

def race_car(name):
    print(f"{name} waiting...")
    start_gate.wait()  # All wait here
    print(f"{name} goes!")

cars = [threading.Thread(target=race_car, args=(f"Car {i}",)) for i in range(5)]
for c in cars: c.start()
time.sleep(1)
print("GREEN LIGHT!")
start_gate.set()  # All start at once
explanation: Event allows one or more threads to wait for a signal from another thread.

title: Threading Queue
code:
import threading
import queue
import time

# Thread-safe queue:
q = queue.Queue(maxsize=10)

def producer():
    for i in range(10):
        item = f"item-{i}"
        q.put(item)
        print(f"Produced: {item}")
        time.sleep(0.2)
    q.put(None)  # Sentinel: signals end

def consumer():
    while True:
        item = q.get()
        if item is None:  # Sentinel received
            break
        print(f"Consumed: {item}")
        time.sleep(0.5)
        q.task_done()

prod = threading.Thread(target=producer)
cons = threading.Thread(target=consumer)
prod.start()
cons.start()
prod.join()
cons.join()

# Queue methods:
q = queue.Queue()
q.put(1, block=True, timeout=5)  # Block with timeout
q.put_nowait(2)                   # Raise Full if full

item = q.get(block=True, timeout=5)  # Block with timeout
item = q.get_nowait()  # Raise Empty if empty
print(q.qsize())  # Approximate size
print(q.empty())  # Is empty?
print(q.full())   # Is full?

# Queue variants:
q_lifo = queue.LifoQueue()  # Stack-like (last in, first out)
q_priority = queue.PriorityQueue()  # Priority-based

# Priority queue:
q_priority.put((1, "low"))
q_priority.put((0, "high"))
q_priority.put((2, "mid"))
print(q_priority.get()[1])  # "high" (lowest priority first)

# Join/wait for all tasks:
q = queue.Queue()
for i in range(5):
    q.put(i)

worker_threads = []
for _ in range(3):
    def worker():
        while True:
            try:
                item = q.get_nowait()
                print(f"Processing {item}")
                q.task_done()
            except queue.Empty:
                break
    t = threading.Thread(target=worker)
    t.start()
    worker_threads.append(t)

q.join()  # Wait until all items are processed
print("All items processed")
explanation: queue.Queue is thread-safe. put()/get() with block+timeout. Join waits for task_done() calls.

title: ThreadPoolExecutor
description: High-level thread pool for concurrent execution
code:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
import time

def fetch_url(url: str) -> tuple:
    time.sleep(1)  # Simulate network
    return (url, len(url))

urls = ["https://example.com", "https://python.org", "https://github.com"]

# Using submit():
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as executor:
    futures = {executor.submit(fetch_url, url): url for url in urls}
    
    for future in as_completed(futures):
        url = futures[future]
        try:
            result = future.result()
            print(f"{url}: {result}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{url} failed: {e}")

# Using map():
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as executor:
    results = list(executor.map(fetch_url, urls))
    print(results)

# Timeout:
with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
    future = executor.submit(fetch_url, "https://example.com")
    try:
        result = future.result(timeout=2)  # Raise TimeoutError if >2s
    except TimeoutError:
        print("Timed out")
        future.cancel()

# ProcessPoolExecutor (CPU-bound tasks):
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

def cpu_intensive(n: int) -> int:
    return sum(i * i for i in range(n))

with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
    results = list(executor.map(cpu_intensive, [10_000_000] * 4))
    print(results)

# Map with timeout:
with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
    results = executor.map(fetch_url, urls, timeout=3)
    try:
        for r in results:
            print(r)
    except TimeoutError:
        print("Map timed out")

# Shutdown (wait=True by default):
executor = ThreadPoolExecutor()
executor.submit(fetch_url, "https://example.com")
executor.shutdown(wait=True)  # Wait for pending futures
explanation: ThreadPoolExecutor manages a thread pool. submit() returns Future. map() for batch processing.

title: Subprocess Module
description: Spawn new processes and interact with them
code:
import subprocess

# Run command and wait:
result = subprocess.run(
    ["ls", "-l", "."],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=True  # Raise CalledProcessError on non-zero exit
)
print(result.stdout)  # Output
print(result.stderr)  # Error (if any)
print(result.returncode)  # 0 (success)

# With shell string:
result = subprocess.run(
    "ls -la | head -3",
    shell=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True
)
print(result.stdout)

# Run without capturing:
subprocess.run(["echo", "hello"])  # Prints to terminal

# Check return code:
try:
    subprocess.run(["false"], check=True)
except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
    print(f"Command failed with code {e.returncode}")

# Get output as string:
output = subprocess.check_output(["echo", "hello"], text=True)
print(output)  # "hello\n"

# Run with timeout:
try:
    subprocess.run(["sleep", "10"], timeout=3)
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    print("Command timed out")

# Popen for full control:
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["grep", "python"],
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    text=True
)
stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(
    "I love python\nJava is ok\npython is great\n"
)
print(f"Output: {stdout}")  # I love python\npython is great

# Environment variables:
result = subprocess.run(
    ["env"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    env={"CUSTOM_VAR": "value"},
    shell=True
)

# Working directory:
result = subprocess.run(
    ["pwd"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    cwd="/tmp"
)
print(result.stdout)  # /tmp
explanation: subprocess.run() for simple cases, Popen() for complex interaction. Use capture_output=True to capture I/O.

title: Async Await Basics
code:
import asyncio

# Coroutine function:
async def greet(name: str, delay: float):
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Run single coroutine:
result = asyncio.run(greet("Alice", 1))
print(result)  # Hello, Alice!

# Run multiple concurrently:
async def main():
    # Run tasks concurrently:
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        greet("Alice", 2),
        greet("Bob", 1),
        greet("Charlie", 3)
    )
    print(results)  # ['Hello, Alice!', 'Hello, Bob!', 'Hello, Charlie!']

asyncio.run(main())

# Create task (background):
async def main():
    task = asyncio.create_task(greet("Background", 2))
    print("Doing other work...")
    result = await task  # Wait for task
    print(result)

# Asynchronous context manager:
class AsyncResource:
    async def __aenter__(self):
        print("Acquiring resource")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        return self
    
    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
        print("Releasing resource")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    
    async def process(self):
        return "Processed"

async def main():
    async with AsyncResource() as res:
        result = await res.process()
        print(result)

# Asynchronous generator:
async def async_range(n):
    for i in range(n):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        yield i

async def main():
    async for num in async_range(5):
        print(num, end=" ")  # 0 1 2 3 4

# Timeout:
async def main():
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(1):
            await greet("Slow", 5)
    except TimeoutError:
        print("Timed out!")
explanation: async def defines coroutines. await suspends until result is ready. asyncio.gather() runs tasks concurrently.

title: Async Web Request
description: Make async HTTP requests using aiohttp
code:
import asyncio
import aiohttp

async def fetch_url(session: aiohttp.ClientSession, url: str) -> dict:
    async with session.get(url) as response:
        return {
            "url": url,
            "status": response.status,
            "size": len(await response.text())
        }

async def main():
    urls = [
        "https://example.com",
        "https://python.org",
        "https://github.com"
    ]
    
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        tasks = [fetch_url(session, url) for url in urls]
        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        
        for result in results:
            if isinstance(result, Exception):
                print(f"Error: {result}")
            else:
                print(f"{result['url']}: {result['status']} ({result['size']} bytes)")

# asyncio.run(main())

# Rate limiting:
import asyncio

class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(self, rate: float):
        self.rate = rate
        self.last = 0
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
    
    async def __aenter__(self):
        async with self.lock:
            now = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
            wait = self.last + 1.0 / self.rate - now
            if wait > 0:
                await asyncio.sleep(wait)
            self.last = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
    
    async def __aexit__(self, *args):
        pass

rate_limiter = RateLimiter(10)  # 10 requests per second

async def rate_limited_fetch(session, url):
    async with rate_limiter:
        return await fetch_url(session, url)
explanation: aiohttp enables async HTTP requests. Use ClientSession and asyncio.gather() for concurrent fetches.

title: Custom Exception
description: Define and raise custom exception classes
code:
class ValidationError(Exception):
    """Raised when data validation fails."""
    pass

class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    """Raised when account has insufficient funds."""
    def __init__(self, balance: float, amount: float):
        self.balance = balance
        self.amount = amount
        super().__init__(f"Insufficient funds: balance={balance}, required={amount}")

class UserNotFoundError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, user_id: int):
        self.user_id = user_id
        super().__init__(f"User with ID {user_id} not found")

def validate_age(age: int):
    if age < 0:
        raise ValidationError(f"Age cannot be negative: {age}")
    if age > 150:
        raise ValidationError(f"Age too high: {age}")

def withdraw(balance: float, amount: float):
    if amount > balance:
        raise InsufficientFundsError(balance, amount)
    return balance - amount

# Usage:
try:
    validate_age(-5)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(f"Validation: {e}")

try:
    withdraw(100, 200)
except InsufficientFundsError as e:
    print(f"Need ${e.amount - e.balance:.2f} more")

# Try assertions:
def process_user(user_id: int):
    assert user_id > 0, f"Invalid user_id: {user_id}"
    # Process...

# Multiple custom exceptions hierarchy:
class AppError(Exception):
    """Base application error."""
    pass

class ConfigError(AppError):
    """Configuration error."""
    pass

class DatabaseError(AppError):
    """Database operation error."""
    pass

class ConnectionError(DatabaseError):
    """Database connection error."""
    pass

# Catch base class:
try:
    raise ConnectionError("Failed to connect")
except DatabaseError as e:  # Also catches ConnectionError
    print(f"Database error: {e}")

# Exception hierarchy division:
# BaseException
# ├── SystemExit
# ├── KeyboardInterrupt
# ├── GeneratorExit
# └── Exception
#     ├── StopIteration
#     ├── ArithmeticError (ZeroDivisionError, ...)
#     ├── LookupError (IndexError, KeyError)
#     ├── ValueError
#     ├── TypeError
#     ├── RuntimeError
#     ├── IOError (FileNotFoundError, ...)
#     └── ...
explanation: Custom exceptions inherit from Exception. Add context via __init__ parameters for better error reporting.

title: With Context Manager File I/O
description: Read and write files using context managers
code:
# Write to file:
with open("output.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Hello, World!\n")
    f.write("Line 2\n")

# Write multiple lines:
lines = ["Line 1\n", "Line 2\n", "Line 3\n"]
with open("output.txt", "w") as f:
    f.writelines(lines)

# Read entire file:
with open("output.txt", "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
    print(content)

# Read line by line:
with open("output.txt", "r") as f:
    for line in f:  # Lazy iteration
        print(line.strip())

# Read all lines:
with open("output.txt", "r") as f:
    lines = f.readlines()  # Returns list of lines

# Append to file:
with open("log.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("New log entry\n")

# Binary mode:
with open("image.jpg", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

with open("output.jpg", "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)

# Read/write mode:
with open("file.txt", "r+") as f:
    content = f.read()
    f.write("Appended text")

# Seek and tell:
with open("file.txt", "r") as f:
    print(f.tell())    # 0 (position)
    data = f.read(10)  # Read 10 bytes
    print(f.tell())    # 10
    f.seek(0)          # Go to beginning
    print(f.read(5))   # Read first 5 bytes

# File modes:
# "r"  — read (default)
# "w"  — write (overwrite)
# "a"  — append
# "r+" — read and write
# "w+" — read and write (overwrite)
# "a+" — read and append
# "rb" — binary read
# "wb" — binary write
# "x"  — exclusive creation (fail if exists)

# Exclusive creation:
try:
    with open("new.txt", "x") as f:
        f.write("Only created if doesn't exist")
except FileExistsError:
    print("File already exists")
explanation: Use 'with open() as f:' for automatic file closing. Modes: r (read), w (write), a (append), b (binary).

title: File Encoding Write Read
description: Read and write files with specific encodings
code:
# Write with encoding:
with open("data.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("Hello, café 日本語 😊\n")

# Read with encoding:
with open("data.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    content = f.read()
    print(content)  # Hello, café 日本語 😊

# Handle encoding errors:
try:
    with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="ascii") as f:
        content = f.read()
except UnicodeDecodeError:
    print("Can't read as ASCII")

# Ignore/replace errors:
with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="ascii", errors="ignore") as f:
    content = f.read()

with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="ascii", errors="replace") as f:
    content = f.read()  # Replaces bad chars with �

# Common encodings:
with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:    # Universal (default)
with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="latin-1") as f:  # Western Europe
with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="cp1252") as f:   # Windows Western
with open("file.txt", "r", encoding="shift-jis") as f: # Japanese

# Read large file in chunks:
def read_in_chunks(filename: str, chunk_size: int = 8192):
    with open(filename, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(chunk_size):
            yield chunk

for chunk in read_in_chunks("large_file.txt"):
    process(chunk)

# Read last N lines of a file:
from collections import deque

def tail(filename: str, n: int = 10):
    with open(filename, "r") as f:
        return list(deque(f, maxlen=n))

last_lines = tail("log.txt", 5)

# Count lines efficiently:
with open("large.txt", "r") as f:
    line_count = sum(1 for _ in f)
    print(f"{line_count} lines")
explanation: Always specify encoding when opening files. utf-8 is the default since Python 3. Use errors='replace' for safety.
